sources.search_query: Switzerland official immigration tourist visa requirements sem.admin.ch nationality
sources.relevant_excerpt: Third-country nationals (non-EU/EFTA) who require a visa must meet the following entry requirements in order to enter Switzerland. The SEM does not issue visas. Swiss representations abroad are responsible for issuing and refusing visas. [Applicants need] a valid C visa (Schengen visa), a valid D visa (national visa), or a valid residence permit from a Schengen country. [The travel document must be] issued less than ten years ago and is valid for at least three months after the date of their intended departure from the Schengen area (for holders of C visas). [Applicants must demonstrate] the purpose and circumstances of their stay in Switzerland [and] sufficient financial means for the duration of their intended stay and for their return. [The page links to the online application at swiss-visa.ch: 'Where and how can I apply for a visa?']

sources.relevant_excerpt: List of visa requirements (legend of V-codes used in Annex CH-1, List 1). V: third-country nationals with valid Schengen residence permits or type D visas plus recognised travel documents are exempt from the visa requirement. V1: visa required for specific work sectors (construction, catering, cleaning, security, erotic services) and any gainful occupation exceeding 8 days within a calendar year. V2: British passport holders' requirements vary by nationality designation (British Citizen has full exemption). V12, V13, V18: visa exemption applies only to biometric passport holders. V14: visa required for passports lacking identity card numbers. V16, V17: apply specifically to Hong Kong and Macao SAR passport holders.

dispositions.maximum_stay: No visa for any length of stay; stays over 90 days require registration/residence permit under EU/EFTA free-movement rules
conditions: Must present valid personal identification: an ID card or a passport
Must not pose a threat to public order and security
Travel document must be valid for at least three months after the intended date of departure from the Schengen area and issued within the last 10 years

Visa exemption is for stays without gainful occupation; for nationalities marked V1 in SEM Annex CH-1 List 1 a visa is required for certain work sectors and for any gainful occupation exceeding 8 days within a calendar year
ALB, BIH, GEO, MDA, MNE, MKD, SRB, UKR: exemption applies only to holders of biometric passports (SEM footnotes V12/V13/V18)
TWN: exemption applies only to Taiwan passports that include an identity card number (SEM footnote V14)
HKG: Hong Kong SAR passport (SEM footnote V16); MAC: Macao SAR passport (SEM footnote V17)
GBR: applies to British Citizen passport holders (SEM footnote V2); other British nationality categories may differ
Must not be listed in the Schengen Information System (SIS) for refusal of entry and must not pose a threat to public order, internal security or public health
Schengen visa type C required for tourist stays of up to 90 days
The SEM does not issue visas; Swiss representations abroad are responsible for issuing and refusing visas
Applications for a category C visa must be submitted online using the application form provided (swiss-visa.ch) or directly to the Swiss representation responsible for the place of residence
Applicant must demonstrate the purpose and circumstances of the stay and sufficient financial means for the stay and return
Travel document issued less than ten years ago and valid for at least three months after intended departure from the Schengen area
Visa-exempt for tourist stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period (DEU and FRA under EU/EFTA free-movement rules); no tourist visa needed
Every nationality not covered by the exemption rows above requires a Schengen visa type C per SEM Annex CH-1 List 1 (complete published list, version of 3 April 2026)
Apply online via swiss-visa.ch or directly to the Swiss representation responsible for the place of residence; visas are issued by Swiss representations abroad

Switzerland operates no tourist eVisa. Applications can be started online (swiss-visa.ch) but visas are issued or refused only by Swiss representations abroad; the channels are visa-free entry or a consular Schengen C visa

As of 2026-07-23 no travel authorisation is required. SEM states ETIAS, a new European travel authorisation system covering Switzerland, launches in the final quarter of 2026 (EUR 20, generally valid 3 years); it is not yet in operation at this snapshot date
No visa-on-arrival channel exists: visa-required travellers must hold a C visa, D visa or Schengen residence permit before entry, and visas are issued only by Swiss representations abroad

policies.policy_name: Overview of ID and visa provisions according to nationality (Annex CH-1, List 1)
policies.description: Switzerland's authoritative nationality-by-nationality list of ID and visa provisions, published by the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM). Nationalities marked 'No' for stays up to 90 days enter visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Footnotes: V1 (visa still required for certain gainful occupation), V2 (British Citizen exemption), V12/V13/V18 (biometric passports only), V14 (Taiwan passport must contain identity card number), V16/V17 (Hong Kong/Macao SAR passports). Complete exempt set recorded in applies_to_nationalities.
conditions: Maximum stay 90 days in any 180-day period for visa-exempt third-country nationals
Travel document valid at least three months after intended departure from the Schengen area and issued within the last 10 years
Exemption does not cover gainful occupation for V1-marked nationalities (visa required for listed work sectors or any employment exceeding 8 days per calendar year)

policies.description: Citizens of EU and EFTA states do not require a visa to enter Switzerland; they enter with a valid ID card or passport under the free-movement rules and need only a registration/residence permit for stays exceeding 90 days.
conditions: Must present valid personal identification, an ID card or a passport
Must not pose a threat to public order and security

policies.policy_name: Schengen visa type C (short stay, incl. tourism)
policies.description: Visa-required nationalities must obtain a Schengen visa type C for tourist stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. The SEM does not issue visas; Swiss representations abroad issue or refuse them. Applications are submitted online via the official swiss-visa.ch online visa system or directly to the competent Swiss representation. Fee EUR 90 (adults) / EUR 45 (children 6-12).
conditions: Demonstrate purpose and circumstances of the stay
Demonstrate sufficient financial means for the stay and the return
Travel document issued less than ten years ago and valid at least three months after intended departure from the Schengen area
Not listed in the Schengen Information System (SIS) for refusal of entry; no threat to public order, internal security or public health

policies.policy_name: ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) - announced, not yet in operation
policies.description: SEM states that ETIAS, a new European travel authorisation system that will cover visa-exempt travellers to the Schengen area including Switzerland, launches in the final quarter of 2026, will cost 20 euros and will generally be valid for 3 years. As of the snapshot date 2026-07-23 it is not in operation and no travel authorisation is required.
conditions: Not yet in operation as of 2026-07-23
